data.narrative:
DigiChem is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Greg Ellson and Ben Berman that has raised $4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector universe comprising 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Given the early stage and limited comparable data, stage-progression methodology was the applicable triangulation approach. Using the $4M in total capital raised as a baseline proxy for seed-stage valuation, application of a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of $10M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrower robotics subsector; the broader sector universe lacked the minimum three datapoints required for meaningful median benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $8M to $12M, with a median point of $10M. This range reflects the mechanical output of stage-progression methodology applied to raised capital. Key uncertainties include the lack of granular private comparable data at seed stage, which constrains confidence in the multiplier assumption, and the heterogeneity of the broader sector peers relative to DigiChem's specific subsector positioning. Additional rounds of comparable company data or revenue-based metrics would materially improve the precision of this estimate.
